$comment: Channel registry: each distribution surface novada-mcp ships to is ONE ROW here, never a
branch in generate.mjs/check.mjs. Adding a channel means adding a row, not editing code.
Field semantics:
path             - repo-relative path to the channel's manifest file (string, or array
of strings for a channel that spans multiple files).
writer_kind      - key into generate.mjs's WRITERS table, or null if this round writes
nothing for this row (verify-only, or nothing owned yet).
owned_fields     - exact pointer/key strings (see version_field/name_field/
description_field) that distribution/generate.mjs is allowed to
WRITE. A field can be present in *_field for VERIFICATION without
being in owned_fields (verified-but-not-generated) — e.g.
claude-code-marketplace's plugin name is checked against
listing.name but never rewritten by this script.
version_field / name_field / description_field / url_field - for a .json path, an
RFC-6901 JSON Pointer (leading '/'); for a .yaml path, a bare
TOP-LEVEL (column 0, unindented) YAML key name. null/absent means
'this channel has no such field' (version_equal / the relevant
legibility check / endpoint_equal skips the row).
url_field        - (brief-F, R1) pointer/key holding this channel's hosted MCP endpoint
URL. check.mjs's endpoint_equal verifies it equals listing.hosted_endpoint
for EVERY row that sets it, regardless of owned_fields membership —
generate.mjs only WRITES it when url_field is also listed in
owned_fields (same owned-vs-verified split as version/name/description).
npm-package/server.json's row sets url_field but deliberately omits it
from owned_fields (verify-only, matching this round's invariant that
gen-server-json.mjs's semantics are not touched here).
required_fields  - (brief-F, R3) object mapping an exact JSON pointer (JSON manifests
only) to a shape expectation object: {must:'exist'}, {must:'not_exist'},
or {must:'equal', value:<literal>}. check.mjs's field_shape check
enforces every entry for every row that sets this field — catches a
channel-specific field-name typo (e.g. Antigravity's serverUrl vs a
stray url key) that no generic version/name/description/url check
would ever see, without a per-channel branch in check.mjs itself.
description_max_len - max character length check.mjs enforces for description_field.
description_derived - true ONLY for a row whose description_field is allowed to contain
a hand-typed tool/platform count (the no-hand-typed-counts legibility
rule is scoped to version_field/name_field/description_field VALUES,
not a whole-file text scan — see distribution/README.md 'Known
scope decisions' for why, and distribution/check.mjs's legibility
comment for the exact mechanism).
generated_by     - 'distribution/generate.mjs' | 'npm-package/scripts/gen-server-json.mjs'
| null. check.mjs's generated_clean check only runs generate.mjs's
--check diff against rows owned by distribution/generate.mjs; a row
owned by gen-server-json.mjs is verified (version/name/description
equality + legibility + location) but never diffed against
generate.mjs's writer output, per this round's invariant that
gen-server-json.mjs's semantics are not to be touched.
install_snippet  - one copy-pasteable install command/sequence for distribution/INSTALL.md.
publish_mechanism- how a change to this file actually reaches the channel (informational;
not enforced by any check).
surface          - (brief-N, 2026-10-19, D1) 'local' | 'hosted' | 'both' — which MCP
endpoint(s) this row's installed artifact actually connects to.
'local': runs the npm package directly (full tool set, incl. browser
automation). 'hosted': only ever talks to listing.hosted_endpoint
(browser automation NOT available — see hosted-server/vercel/api/
mcp.ts's HOSTED_HIDDEN). 'both': one listing spans both (e.g. mcp-
registry's server.json). Drives which of listing.json's two
description variants (description | description_hosted) generate.mjs's
resolveDescriptionForRow writes, and what check.mjs's surface_claims
check enforces. Omitted only for a row with no description_field at all
(nothing to classify). check.mjs's surface_derived_consistent check
(brief-N R2 fix, 2026-10-19, round 2 review) cross-checks this DECLARED
value against a DERIVED one read out of the row's own manifest content
(a url_field resolving to a real URL = hosted signal; a stdio
startCommand/packages[].transport = local signal) — closes the gap where
hand-relabeling ONLY this field (leaving the manifest's real endpoint
untouched) silently defeated surface_claims.
surface_peers    - (brief-N R2 fix, 2026-10-19, round 2 review) optional array of other row
ids whose manifest content ALSO counts toward THIS row's derived surface
— for the few channels split across two files with disjoint schemas
(antigravity-plugin/antigravity-mcp-config, openai-codex-plugin/openai-
codex-mcp-config) where the description-bearing file itself (plugin.json)
carries no url/startCommand signal of its own; the real endpoint wiring
lives in the sibling file. Explicit and data-declared, never directory-
guessed — npm-package/ alone holds 3 unrelated channel manifests (mcp-
registry/glama/smithery) in one folder, so 'same directory' would wrongly
union their signals.
kind             - (brief-N, 2026-10-19, D2) absent for every normal row (a manifest file
that lives IN this repo). 'external' marks a row whose real manifest
lives in a DIFFERENT repository — this repo never writes to it, only
verifies it over the network (see external_repo). check.mjs's
isExternalRow(row) exempts it from the three checks that assume a LOCAL
file exists at row.path: location_rules, shape_declared, ci_paths_cover.
external_repo    - (brief-N, 2026-10-19, D2) required when kind:"external". {owner, repo,
ref, marketplace_path, plugin_path, mcp_config_path,
expected_plugin_name, mcp_url_field} — check.mjs's
external_repo_consistent check fetches
raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<ref>/<marketplace_path|
plugin_path|mcp_config_path> and asserts marketplace.json exists,
plugin.json's name equals expected_plugin_name, and mcp_config_path's
mcp_url_field (a JSON pointer) equals listing.hosted_endpoint.
brief-I (2026-10-15, I1 CRITICAL): a manifest's content was previously a parsed-and-
round-tripped object (json-owned-fields/yaml-owned-fields writers only overwrite the
fields they own; every OTHER key in the file — including one an attacker injected —
round-trips untouched) checked only against an ALLOWLIST of individual field pointers,
which has no notion of 'no other keys may exist here' at all. Every row now declares
EXACTLY ONE of two closed-shape mechanisms (enforced by check.mjs's new shape_declared
meta-check, which fails a row declaring neither):
writer_kind "json-full" - for a row whose file is FULLY determined by this generator
(nothing hand-authored survives it). `full_template` is the row's
complete expected object, in exact key order; a string leaf matching
`{{token}}` resolves to `token==="version"` -> package.json's version,
`token==="name"` -> the row's resolved name (name_override or
listing.name), or `listing.json[token]` for any other token (e.g.
`{{description}}`, `{{hosted_endpoint}}`, `{{homepage}}`,
`{{repository}}`) — an unresolvable token throws loudly rather than
silently writing the literal string. Every other string/number/array/
object value in `full_template` is a LITERAL, written verbatim. This
replaces json-owned-fields/yaml-owned-fields' partial parse-and-merge
for these rows: generate.mjs rebuilds the WHOLE file from the template
every run, and check.mjs's generated_clean compares the committed
file's exact text against that rebuild — an injected/extra key (or a
removed one) makes the committed file differ from the rebuild and
FAILS, with no allowlist of individually-checked pointers to slip
past. `owned_fields` does not apply to a json-full row (the whole file
is implicitly owned) and is omitted from these rows.
closed_shape      - for a row with genuinely hand-authored content this generator does
NOT fully rebuild (server.json, marketplace.json, smithery.yaml,
glama.json — three of these also keep an independent owned_fields/
writer_kind for the ONE field they do own, e.g. smithery's top-level
`description`; closed_shape is additive, not a replacement for that).
Maps an object path to the list of keys permitted there — `""` is the
file's top-level object/mapping; `"/x/*"` (JSON) iterates every
element of the array at `/x`; a bare YAML key name (e.g.
`"startCommand"`) is that key's own direct children, one level deep.
A path that does not resolve in a given file (e.g. a row's fixture
has no `/packages` array at all) is silently skipped for THAT path —
closed_shape enforces 'nothing extra where this structure exists', not
'this structure must exist' (that is a `required_fields`/
`pinned_fields` job). `pinned_fields` maps one exact pointer (JSON) or
`topKey.childKey` (YAML, one level of nesting) to its exact required
literal value — for EXECUTION-RELEVANT fields an attacker could tamper
with even while staying inside the allowed key set (smithery's
`startCommand.type`/`startCommand.commandFunction` — the literal
shell command Smithery runs on the end user's machine; server.json's
`packages[0].identifier`/`packages[0].transport.type`/
`remotes[0].type`/`remotes[0].url`). A pointer that does not resolve
(missing) counts as a mismatch against its expected literal — unlike
closed_shape's path lookup, a declared pinned_fields entry IS a
'must exist with exactly this value' assertion.
brief-J (2026-10-15, J1 CRITICAL): three red-team rounds in a row found a NEW hole in
closed_shape's own hand-written allowlist (an injected array ELEMENT — packages[1]/
remotes[1]/plugins[1] — built entirely from already-allowed keys; a key nested deeper than
closed_shape's own declared path, e.g. smithery.yaml's startCommand.configSchema.properties;
an allowed-but-unpinned key's VALUE, e.g. server.json's packages[0].registryType) because an
allowlist only ever covers paths someone thought of. Two additions, both table-driven:
`pinned_array_lengths` maps an exact array JSON pointer to its required length (closes the
array-length half of the injected-element attack; JSON manifests only, same scope as
required_fields) — kept alongside pinned_fields as readable, defense-in-depth intent, not a
replacement for it. The GENERIC backstop underneath both is check.mjs's new `tamper_evident`
check: every closed_shape row's current file(s) are hashed via generate.mjs's
canonicalFormForRow (stable-sorted JSON, or the YAML text verbatim, with ONLY the row's own
version/name/description/url field VALUES neutralized — everything else, including an
array's length and anything nested at any depth, is part of the hash) and compared against
distribution/pinned-hashes.json, a small machine-maintained ledger (never hand-edited, same
spirit as a lockfile) keyed by row id. A mismatch fails with a fix hint naming
`node distribution/generate.mjs --repin <row-id>` — which prints the old/new hash AND a line
diff of the hand-authored content it is about to accept, so a legitimate edit is a reviewed,
visible action, never a silent rubber-stamp. This closes the attack CLASS (any future
structural change anywhere in a closed_shape row's file), not just the three concrete holes
named above.
brief-J (2026-10-15, J5 LOW): manifest_patterns also matches `.cursor/mcp.json`,
`.vscode/mcp.json`, and bare `mcp.json` (no leading dot — distinct from the existing
`.mcp.json` pattern, which only matches a DOTTED filename) so a stray editor/IDE MCP client
config dropped anywhere in the repo is flagged by no_orphans instead of going unnoticed.
brief-K (2026-10-15, K1 CRITICAL): `claude-code-marketplace`'s `plugins[0].source.url`/`.sha`
had NO pin at all — closed_shape's top-level allowlist and pinned_array_lengths bound this
file's own key SET and plugins[] LENGTH, but neither field's VALUE was ever checked, so a
diff that swapped `source.url` to a fork AND re-ran `--repin` (updating tamper_evident's own
baseline to accept the tampered content) passed every check. Two new, table-driven pin
mechanisms (check.mjs's closed_shape adds both, alongside the existing pinned_fields):
`pinned_fields_template` maps a pointer to a string that may embed one or more `{{token}}`
placeholders (resolved via generate.mjs's `resolveTemplateString` against
distribution/listing.json + package.json's version — the SAME templating syntax
full_template already uses, generalized to allow a placeholder embedded inside a larger
literal, e.g. `"{{repository}}.git"`) — an EXACT-equality check against a DYNAMICALLY
DERIVED expectation, so a future listing.json repository rename updates this pin
automatically with zero channels.json edit, instead of a second hand-duplicated literal
that could itself drift. `pinned_fields_format` maps a pointer to a regular-expression
string — a FORMAT pin for a field whose exact VALUE legitimately changes release-over-
release (a git commit sha) but whose SHAPE never should (40 lowercase hex characters).
Neither mechanism can be defeated by re-running `--repin` the way tamper_evident's hash
alone could, because both are evaluated dynamically against the CURRENT listing.json/regex
at check time, independent of whatever is recorded in pinned-hashes.json. NOTE (brief-N,
2026-10-19): `claude-code-marketplace` (this bullet's original example row) was retired by
D2 below — `mcp-registry`'s `/remotes/0/url`/`/packages/0/version` now carry these same two
mechanisms instead (see that row), so the worked example moved but the mechanism itself is
unchanged.
brief-N (2026-10-19 — independent review of PR #20, 3 owner decisions, class-not-instance):
D1 'surface' (HIGH): a shared description string was interpolated into every row alike,
which was ACCURATE for a row that runs the full local npm package but OVERCLAIMED for a
row that only ever talks to the hosted endpoint (hosted-server/vercel/api/mcp.ts's
HOSTED_HIDDEN excludes novada_browser/novada_browser_flow there). Every row now declares
`surface`: "local" (installs/runs the npm package directly — the full tool set, including
browser automation), "hosted" (only ever connects to listing.hosted_endpoint — browser
automation is NOT available), or "both" (one listing spans both paths, e.g. mcp-registry's
single server.json carries a local packages[] AND a hosted remotes[] entry — its description
must stay true for BOTH, not pick one). distribution/listing.json gained a second variant,
`description_hosted` (no browser-automation clause) alongside the original `description`
(kept true for "local"/"both" by scoping the clause to the local package, see that file's
own $comment_surfaces); distribution/generate.mjs's `resolveDescriptionForRow` picks between
them by `row.surface`, in both `ownedValuesFor` (json-owned-fields/yaml-owned-fields rows)
and `resolveFullTemplatePlaceholder` (json-full rows' `{{description}}` token) — ONE
resolution function, not a per-writer-kind branch. check.mjs's new `surface_claims` check
is the generic backstop: it fails if a `surface:"hosted"` row's CURRENT generated
description text mentions a HOSTED_HIDDEN tool's capability phrase, driven by parsing
HOSTED_HIDDEN itself (never a hardcoded list) — adding a tool to HOSTED_HIDDEN with a known
capability phrase extends coverage by a new table ROW in check.mjs, not a new branch. A
`surface:"local"` row keeping the phrase is the documented mirror case (not a violation).
gen-server-json.mjs's own server.json description template (verify-only, not generate.mjs-
owned — see that row's `description_derived_reason`) was hand-reworded to the same
truthfulness bar: 'browser via npm', scoping the claim instead of dropping or overclaiming it.
D2 'kind: external' (CRITICAL): `claude-code-plugin`/`claude-code-marketplace` (npm-package/
.claude-plugin/) shipped NO MCP server wiring at all (no .mcp.json anywhere in that
directory) and sat at a path (`npm-package/.claude-plugin/`) the `/plugin marketplace add
<owner>/<repo>` CLI form can never read (the marketplace root must be the git repo ROOT).
A separate, already-working, review-hardened repo (NovadaLabs/claude-plugins) is the real,
canonical Claude Code distribution channel. Both rows are REMOVED (git history keeps the
retired files; a fresh checkout of this commit no longer ships npm-package/.claude-plugin/
at all) and replaced by ONE new row, `claude-plugins-external`, carrying `"kind":
"external"` and an `external_repo` block ({owner, repo, ref, marketplace_path, plugin_path,
mcp_config_path, expected_plugin_name, mcp_url_field}) — this repo never writes to that
repo (no push/PR), it only VERIFIES it, over the network, via check.mjs's new
`external_repo_consistent` check (raw.githubusercontent.com, 3 files: marketplace.json
exists at the external repo's root; its plugin's name matches; its plugin's .mcp.json URL
equals listing.hosted_endpoint). `kind:"external"` is a table-driven exemption, not a
row.id branch: `isExternalRow(row)` short-circuits exactly the three per-row checks that
assume a LOCAL file (`location_rules`, `shape_declared`, `ci_paths_cover`) — every other
check already no-ops naturally for a row with no version_field/url_field/closed_shape/
required_fields set, which this row deliberately leaves unset. The external check itself
is network-scoped to the REAL repo root only (`ctx.root === ROOT`) so the shared test-suite
fixture (a tmpdir, never the real root) never pays a network round-trip or timeout just to
exercise an unrelated check; its pure assertion logic (`evaluateExternalRepoManifests`) is
unit-tested directly against synthetic fetched-text, and MUST fail loudly (never silently
pass) when the network is unreachable AND `process.env.CI` is set — it may only skip (with
a printed reason) on an unreachable network locally.
D3 'dify-plugin'/'dify-provider': distribution/dify/ (PR #21) shipped with no channels.json
row at all — manifest.yaml/provider/novada.yaml were invisible to no_orphans (not in
manifest_patterns) and distribution/dify/README.md's tool table was invisible to
claims_consistent (no claim_surfaces entry), the exact class of gap R10 closed for every
OTHER channel. Two new rows (ONE ROW PER FILE — manifest.yaml and provider/novada.yaml have
completely disjoint top-level key sets, the same `claude-code-plugin`/`claude-code-
marketplace` precedent applied), both `version_field: null` (Dify version bumps are
independent of this monorepo's package.json BY DESIGN — each bump is its own Marketplace
PR, and this plugin is a thin client; see each row's `version_field_reason`), both carrying
a `closed_shape` top-level allowlist (hand-authored YAML, same `writer_kind: null`/
`generated_by: null` shape as the `glama` row). `manifest.yaml` and `provider/novada.yaml`
are now in `manifest_patterns`, claimed by these two rows — `no_orphans` fails if either
row is removed while the files remain (mirror test). `distribution/dify/README.md` is now a
`claim_surfaces` entry with `fact_overrides: {tools: "dify_tools"}` — a NEW fact,

`distribution/dify/utils/tools_table.py`'s own `TOOLS` tuple length and
`provider/novada.yaml`'s `tools:` list, both independently 7 today) — a wrong count in that

claim_surfaces_$comment: brief-F R10 (2026-10-15): the count-drift CLASS (README/landing pages hand-stating a tool/
platform/scraper count that drifts from the built registry — exactly how plugin.json's
'scrape 13 platforms' bug started) was invisible to every check above, which only ever look
at channels.json's OWN rows' manifest fields, never at prose docs. claim_surfaces is a flat
list of glob patterns (matched relative to the repo root, '**' = any depth including zero —
see distribution/check.mjs's claimSurfaceMatcher) naming every prose surface that is allowed
to state one of these counts; claims (below) maps each narrow noun this project actually uses
to the fact key it must equal. check.mjs's claims_consistent scans every surface for a literal
'<N>(+)? <noun>' occurrence and fails if N != the fact's current value, UNLESS the same line
also contains the literal opt-out marker 'claims-ignore' (case-insensitive) — for historical/
changelog prose that is correctly describing a PAST count, or a line whose number denotes a
deliberately different metric that happens to share this project's noun (e.g. the Scraper
API's own, larger, unrelated platform count) and needs a human to confirm/reword rather than
have this check guess. Nouns are deliberately narrow (tools / per-platform scrapers /
platforms only) so this never matches unrelated prose like '195 countries' or '100M+ IPs'.
brief-H (2026-10-15, class-not-instance): fact scope is a property of the SURFACE, not a
single global constant, so an entry here may be a {glob, fact_overrides, reason} object
instead of a bare glob string. fact_overrides maps one claims fact key (e.g. 'tools') to a
DIFFERENT fact key this surface must be checked against instead (e.g. 'hosted_tools') —
hosted-server/landing pages legitimately describe the 28-tool HOSTED subset, not the 37-tool
local-package total, using the same word 'tools' README.md uses for the total. A bare glob
string is unchanged shorthand for 'no override, check every claims noun against its plain
fact' — every pre-brief-H entry still works verbatim. An override naming a fact key
computeFacts() doesn't produce is a loud, thrown config error (see check.mjs's
normalizeClaimSurface/checkClaimsConsistent), never a silent pass, so a typo here can't
quietly disable this check for a whole surface. A surface claim this check still has no fact
or override for (e.g. the Scraper API's own, larger, unrelated platform count) still needs
either the opt-out marker or a reword avoiding the bare noun, exactly as before.
brief-I (2026-10-15, I2/I3/I4): three extensions, all additive to the matching above.
I2 — claims nouns were ASCII-only, so a CJK claim surface's own-language count (e.g.
hosted-server/landing/chat.html's zh span) was invisible to this check even though its
English sibling on the SAME page was checked. A `claims` entry may now carry a `unit`
field (e.g. `{noun_pattern:"工具", fact:"tools", unit:"个"}`) — matched by check.mjs as
`<digits><unit><<=6 non-digit characters, lazy><noun>` (e.g. "26 个网络数据工具"), a bounded
generalization of the brief's own literal `(\d+)\s*个(工具|平台|爬虫)` needed because the
real repo's CJK claims carry a short compound-adjective infix between the measure word and
the noun ("网络数据", "web-data") the same way the English sibling line does — a strictly
adjacent-only match would silently miss the one real instance this finding exists for.
I3 — the English match was adjacent-only (`<N> <noun>` with nothing between), which missed
`docs/TOOLS.md`'s real "16 supported platforms (~87 operations)" instance. check.mjs now
allows up to 2 intervening words from a DELIBERATELY NARROW, verified-safe adjective list
(`supported|working|MCP|data`) between the number and the noun. This list is narrower than
an earlier draft that also included `typed`/`dedicated`/`per-platform`/`web-data`: grepping
every claim_surfaces file before implementing found those four would ALSO newly match
README.md:76/npm-package/README.md:204's "14 typed per-platform tools" (a CORRECT,
pre-existing count of the per-platform SCRAPER tools — 14 — wrongly checked against the
37-tool whole-catalog fact because the literal noun used is "tools", not "scrapers") and
hosted-server/landing/og-image-spec.md's stale "25 web-data tools" (a doc-spec file outside
this round's edit scope) — both would have been new, UNFIXABLE-within-scope failures,
violating this round's own 'only tools.html claim failures may remain' requirement. Kept
narrow on purpose; a future round can widen it again alongside a fix/marker for whichever
newly-caught surface that widening exposes, with its own evidence.
I4 — the `claims-ignore` opt-out marker previously silenced ANY claim on its line with zero
justification required. check.mjs now requires the exact syntax `claims-ignore: <reason>`
with a reason of at least 10 characters (after stripping a trailing HTML-comment closer);
a bare/under-justified marker no longer suppresses the claim AND is itself reported as a
new `claims_consistent(invalid_marker)` failure. check.mjs's CLI also prints every
currently-valid marker's file:line (and reason) as a summary line so a reviewer can see
every suppression in one place instead of hunting through the whole diff.
brief-J (2026-10-15, J3 HIGH): INVERTED from opt-in to opt-out. claim_surfaces used to be the
ONLY way a file got scanned at all — npm-package/ARCHITECTURE.md:55's stale "15 platforms"
(truth 14), the whole of npm-package/skills/**, and the whole of npm-package/docs/** were
structurally invisible by omission, forever, no matter how stale they drifted. check.mjs's
claims_consistent and collectClaimsIgnoreMarkers now scan every file `git ls-files` reports
as TRACKED under *.md/*.html/*.txt (any depth) MINUS `claim_excludes` (below) — a new,
parallel list in the exact shape of `known_orphans`: `{glob, reason}`, one entry per

reason-less or malformed entry, same posture as normalizeClaimSurface's existing config
validation). claim_surfaces keeps its I1/brief-H `fact_overrides` role UNCHANGED (a surface
needing a DIFFERENT fact than the default plain one) but no longer gates inclusion at all —
a bare glob string with no override now carries zero information under this model, so the
two that existed (`README.md`, `npm-package/README.md`, `docs/**/*.md`) were removed; every
remaining entry sets a real fact_overrides. A file matching NO claim_surfaces entry is still
scanned, just with no override (every noun checked against its plain fact) — exactly what a
bare-string entry used to mean. Excluded categories, each with its own reason below: a
historical changelog/report describing a PAST state (CHANGELOG.md, docs/review/**,
docs/evaluation/**, docs/plans/**, dated REFLECTION-*/COMPETITIVE_INTELLIGENCE/test-log
files, the HTML changelog twin, internal handoff/status/runbook logs whose own run-log
sections are dated entries); a mirrored third-party API reference whose counts describe
THAT API's own metric, not this project's registry (npm-package/docs/novada-api/**, the
sibling Developer-API-requirements/reference files, BACKEND_ISSUES.md); an evaluator
prompt/spec comparing novada-mcp against a COMPETITOR's own counts (MCP_TESTING_MANDATE.md,
TEST_PLAYBOOK.md); literal agent-session prompts/transcripts from past development rounds
(npm-package/prompts/**); and golden TEST FIXTURES (hosted-server/scripts/golden/**) — this
finding's own named exclude categories. Every remaining file (README.md, npm-package/
README.md, docs/TOOLS.md, npm-package/ARCHITECTURE.md, npm-package/skills/**,
npm-package/docs/llms.txt, npm-package/docs/novada-mcp-documentation.md, hosted-server/
vercel/README.md, every hosted-server/landing/** page, ...) is now scanned for real, with
any genuinely-different-metric line (a worked example loading a SMALLER tool subset; a
catalog total including 0-op platforms; a line mixing the hosted count and the whole-catalog
